topic: Which existing logic in the spec-kit workflows can be hardened, based on every finding from three prior reads, including the findings nobody turned into a recommendation? Inputs: specs/system-speckit/spec-authoring-and-continuity/005-goldfish-cold-read-plan-review/scratch/prior-reads.md and specs/system-speckit/spec-authoring-and-continuity/005-goldfish-cold-read-plan-review/research/research.md. Targets: .skilled/commands/speckit/assets/speckit-plan.yaml, speckit-implement.yaml and speckit-complete.yaml. Known leads to confirm or refute by reading the lines: (1) the pre-implementation gate passes at 75 of 100 with plan_clarity scored zero, and plan_clarity has no scoring definition; (2) other gate check ids may be scored with no definition, and other thresholds may let a zero on one check pass; (3) checkpoints marked applies_to confirm are skipped in auto mode, so a review nobody reads may guard nothing; (4) confidence scores are given by the session that wrote the document; (5) plan, implement and complete carry copies of the same steps and gates that may have drifted apart; (6) the DEVIATION marker and debug delegation are required by the workflow but almost never appear in specs/; (7) recommend-level.sh may run on only one path; (8) research/research.md is listed as generated by planning but is optional and mostly absent. For each lead and each new one you find: state whether it is a real defect with file and line, the smallest change to an existing line that hardens it, the spec levels it touches, and whether fixing it is worth it or overengineering. Sweep all three files for the same class of defect. Rank the confirmed defects by the damage they allow. Do not propose new commands, agents, documents or metrics files.

focus: Gate arithmetic and gate ownership in speckit-implement.yaml
